subject: On-prem GPU pool population + surge handling playbook
messages:

Subject: On-prem GPU pool population + surge handling playbook

Hey team,

We have the DataStream PoC ramp next quarter and their legal/procurement asks for a private VPC deployment with predictable throughput and documented surge behavior. I want a concise plan we can send to them that covers: sizing for steady-state throughput, growth/surge buffer, warm-pool population strategy, KV/prefix cache warmup, and graceful degradation policies. High-level constraints:

- Target steady throughput: 1200 concurrent requests (avg 1.2s per request) ~ target 2500 tokens/sec sustained across model ensemble.
- Peak surge: up to 4x sustained for short windows (5-15min) during batch ingestion periods.
- On-prem cluster: 8x A100-equivalent nodes initially (customer will consider expansion).

Please reply with numbers (GPU counts, headroom %, prefill approach) and a short ops playbook (what to run during cutover and how to detect/mitigate overload). Attach any spreadsheet/diagram. I need a draft to share with DataStream by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Private Deployments

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: On-prem GPU pool population + surge handling playbook

Lauren — quick sizing sketch below (numbers meant as starting point, will validate with perf traces):

1) Steady-state sizing
- Baseline perf: YOLO-13B-like model running on A100-eq yields ~120 tokens/sec per GPU under our optimized runtime with KV cache hot.
- For 2500 tokens/sec sustained -> ~21 GPUs hot. Round up to 24 GPUs to simplify allocation and allow even shard distribution.

2) Surge buffer
- Short surge (4x): want to absorb 60s spikes primarily via hot spare pool + admission control. For 4x of 2500 = 10k tokens/sec -> need 84 GPUs if all hot. That's unrealistic to keep hot on-prem.
- Strategy: keep 24 GPUs hot, 12 GPUs warm (fast boot/attach), and rely on model fallback/quantized variants for overflow. With admission control (reject heavy-context requests, degrade to 8-bit variant), effective capacity during surge ~48-60 GPUs equivalent.

3) Warm pool & prefill
- Warm pool size: 12 GPUs (1/2 of initial cluster) with model binaries loaded and KV cache prefilled for the top 50 most common prefixes. Background prefill process will run during off-peak and right after deploy.
- Prefill approach: incremental KV-prefill tasks that simulate likely prompt prefixes from production trace (warmup workers running at low QPS).

4) Autoscaling cadence
- Scale decision window: 30s-60s sampling, 3 consecutive windows to trigger scale-up. Warm pool attach time target: <90s for full readiness, <30s for binary-loaded but KV-cold.

5) Monitoring & SLOs
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec consumed, queue depth, GPU utilization, KV hit rate. Alerts: sustained queue > 50 for 2m -> emergency throttle.

I attached a quick capacity model (gpu_capacity_model.xlsx). I can run more detailed sims if we agree on the workload distribution.

- Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime

Adding networking and data-path constraints that change the math:

- Egress/Ingress: customer rack uplinks are 100Gbps. At peak surge (10k tokens/sec, average token payload 200 bytes including protobuf+metadata), that's ~1.6 Gbps — well under 100G but consider bursts and other tenants. Leave 30% headroom -> plan for 3 Gbps sustained for inference egress.

- KV cache implications: prefilled KV increases memory pressure; ensure each GPU has at least 64GB HBM reserved for model + 8-16GB host RAM for KV mapping. If customer nodes are lower-memory variants, we must reduce prefill set and rely more on network-based KV fetch.

- NIC and NUMA layout: warm attach must ensure GPU-local NVLink paths preserved. Attach scripts must validate CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and NUMA affinities. Failure modes documented in ops checklist.

- Observability: packet-level counters and TCPOPT tracing for slow clients (we've seen stalled connections create headroom illusions).

I'll add a network topology diagram (network_topology.drawio) and a short checklist for NIC tuning.

- Irene
Network Reliability Lead

Draft ops playbook and runbook (high level) — attaching ops-warmup-checklist.md with commands/health checks. Key callouts: 

1) Pre-cutover (48-72h before soft launch)
- Load model binaries on warm pool, run integrity checks.
- Run KV prefill job for top-50 prefixes (prefill run at 0.1x expected QPS to avoid saturating network).
- Smoke tests: 200 concurrent synthetic requests using typical prompt shapes (short and long tail).

2) Cutover day
- Bring warm pool online in phases: 4 GPUs every 5 minutes, verify avg latency delta <10% after each step.
- Circulate a temporary routing rule: route 10% of traffic to the new cluster (canary) then 25/50/100.

3) Surge handling during live traffic
- If queue depth > 30 for 3 consecutive 30s windows -> enable admission control and start adding warm GPUs.
- If queue continues to rise after warm attach -> enable 8-bit fallback model and cap request context length to 512 tokens for overflow traffic.

4) Recovery and post-surge
- Run KV re-warm for any GPUs that were cold; schedule background prefill.
- Capture traces and create a post-mortem if headroom was insufficient.

I've added run commands and the small health-check script to the attachment. Also added a simple cost estimate row in the spreadsheet.

- Marissa
Director, Cloud Ops

Maya — answers inline and next steps: 

1) KV prefill time
- Top-50 prefixes on 12 GPUs at 0.1x QPS prefill rate: ~18-25 minutes to reach a usable hitrate; to fully saturate to our target cache hit % expect ~90 minutes. We'll include a two-phase prefill plan (fast-prefill for cutover, background fill for 24h).

2) 8-bit fallback latency delta
- In our tests the 8-bit quantized variant increases p95 by ~10-20% vs baseline but reduces GPU memory usage by 30-40%, allowing more concurrent in-flight requests. We'll include comparative p50/p95 numbers in the next revision.

3) On-call rotation
- Redwood will provide an SRE contact list for 24/7 escalation during PoC: Primary on-call: Marissa Cole; Secondary: Grace O'Connor; Tertiary: Karthik Iyer. We'll send the on-call runbook and phone tree.

- Irene: add NIC tuning and NVLink verification to the drawio and ops checklist (owner: irene) — due tomorrow.
- Marissa: finalize ops-warmup-checklist.md and escalate procedures (owner: marissa) — due tomorrow.

I'll package everything into a single PDF and send to your SREs after we have the updated spreadsheet and diagrams.

Thanks all — nice work pulling together the pieces.
